claims.claim: The forever block repeatedly runs its body in the background and yields to other code, so it should not be described as preventing event handlers from running.

show string displays text on the LED screen and scrolls left when the text exceeds the display; its optional interval parameter is milliseconds per one-LED slide, with larger values scrolling more slowly.
show icon displays the selected LED icon, and its optional interval is the display time in milliseconds with a default of 600 ms.
pause takes a duration in milliseconds, so 500 ms is half a second and 1000 ms is one second.
An if/then/else conditional runs the then branch when its condition is true and the else branch when it is not, allowing the two outcomes to be specified separately.

The on shake block is input.onGesture(Gesture.Shake, handler), an event handler triggered by the shake gesture; available gesture choices also include orientation, tilt, free-fall, 3g, and 6g gestures.
The pick random block maps to randint(min, max) and returns a pseudo-random integer including both endpoints, so randint(1, 3) can produce 1, 2, or 3.
input.acceleration(dimension) returns acceleration in milli-g for x, y, z, or combined strength, with a flat screen-up micro:bit reporting approximately x=0, y=0, z=-1023, and strength=1023.
